structured_output.hypothesis: In the GloNAF checklists, the number of European-native plant species naturalised in the La Plata region (Argentina and Uruguay) and in Australia far exceeds the number of southern-hemisphere-native species naturalised in European regions, and the La Plata excess is larger than the Australian one.
structured_output.pass_criterion: Let E_LP and E_AU be the counts of European-native vascular plant taxa naturalised in Argentina plus Uruguay and in Australia. Let S_EU be the count of taxa native only to the southern hemisphere (South America south of the equator, southern Africa, Australasia) that are naturalised in at least one European GloNAF region. The claim passes if E_LP / S_EU >= 10 AND E_AU / S_EU >= 5 AND E_LP >= E_AU (after normalising by the size of the source continent's native flora if possible).
structured_output.fail_criterion: The claim fails if E_LP / S_EU < 3 or E_AU / S_EU < 3. It also fails if S_EU exceeds 10% of E_LP, so that southern forms are not 'extremely few'. The 'lesser degree in Australia' component fails if E_AU > 1.5 x E_LP.
structured_output.interpretation: Darwin's 'naturalised' corresponds to GloNAF's status of naturalised (established, self-sustaining) alien taxa. His 'European productions' and 'southern forms' are taxa whose native range lies in Europe or the southern hemisphere. His 'La Plata' is Argentina plus Uruguay. His 'in a lesser degree in Australia' is Australia's regional lists. 'Partly displaced the natives' cannot be measured from checklists, so the test covers only the naturalisation asymmetry. Darwin spoke of all organisms but mostly plants, so this is a plant-only test. Modern data record many more taxa than Darwin knew, so the test checks the direction and magnitude of the asymmetry, not his 1859 counts. Native-range assignment would come from the native-range fields GloNAF provides or from a joined external source such as the World Checklist of Vascular Plants.
